title: Adaptive dispatch and fast-path for embedding latency stabilization
creator: Ethan Morales
description:
Problem: Production embedding endpoints show intermittent high tail latency (p99 spikes) under mixed sequence-length workloads. Existing micro-batching scheduler leaves long-sequence requests on the slow path, and kernel selection heuristics sometimes route small batches to suboptimal kernels.

Goal: Stabilize p99 latency for the embeddings endpoint and reduce variability without regressing throughput or cost. Target metrics: p99 <= -25% from baseline, p95 <= -15%, maintain p50 within 5% of current baseline. Preserve overall token/sec throughput within 5%.

Scope: Implement an adaptive dispatch layer that introduces: (1) a short-sequence "fast lane" that prioritizes latency-sensitive requests into tight microbatches with tuned kernels; (2) dynamic kernel hinting based on observed sequence-length and batch shape; (3) a background probe to identify harmful batch compositions and apply per-model routing hints. Work includes telemetry, unit and perf tests, canary rollout and rollback strategy.

Approach / Deliverables:
- Instrument per-request metadata (seq_len, token_distribution, enqueue_time) and add histogram buckets to Grafana dashboards.
- Implement a fast-path dispatcher that forms low-latency microbatches (target 4-8 requests) for sequences <= 256 tokens and short-circuit to optimized kernel variants.
- Add kernel-hint API (runtime-level flag) so scheduler can request single-request kernels for pathological shapes and prefer fused kernels for uniform short batches.
- Introduce adaptive backpressure: when tail variance exceeds threshold, temporarily escalate new short requests into the fast lane and hold long requests for larger batches.
- Create A/B canary with 1% traffic -> 10% -> 50% with automated rollback on error or metric regression.

Non-goals: Full rewrite of batching engine, changes to user-facing SDKs, embedding model architecture changes.

Risks & Mitigations:
- Risk: Fast-path increases cost due to smaller batch sizes. Mitigation: autoscaling knobs and cost telemetry; only enable fast lane under tail spikes and for premium customers initially.
- Risk: Kernel mismatch causing regressions. Mitigation: expanded kernel-suite unit tests + nightly perf matrix on representative shapes.

Success criteria:
- p99 embedding latency improvement >= 25% under our standard mixed-workload trace (2k requests, seq_len distribution attached).
- No more than 5% throughput regression and no encoding errors introduced.
- Safe canary with automated rollback on 2 consecutive 5-minute windows of metric regression.
updates: 2026-02-16: Profiling pass completed on canary fleet; identified that 18% of p99 events are caused by long-seq interleaving in small batches.
2026-02-18: Prototype dispatcher implemented (fast-lane + kernel-hint API). Benchmarks on dev-gpu show p99 improvement of ~18% for short-heavy traffic shapes.

2026-02-22: Kernel hinting tests added for fused vs. single-request kernels; found a 2-3% regression in throughput for some shapes — added heuristic to fallback when utilization drops below threshold.
2026-02-25: Staging canary (1% traffic) deployed with basic telemetry. No customer-visible errors; early p99 drop of 20% on staging trace.
2026-03-01: Expanded canary rollout plan and created automated alerting rule for p95/p99 regressions. Next: increase to 10% and run overnight stability job. PR opened: runtime #7852.
